name: Milestone 12: packs, textures and PBR
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent
Type: task

Done when a Pack unloads and the next loads with no stale id drawn, and Kula plays three textured, sky-lit levels with no magenta.

Decided in the Milestone 12 grilling on 2026-10-14. Pong is out of scope (ntbh6adj). The Kula look is in games/kula/SPEC.md (Look).

## Problem Statement

A game cannot change what is loaded while it runs. The host loads every mesh in assets/meshes/ once, before init, and keeps it for the whole run. Kula needs a different block set and sky for each Theme. A larger game needs to stream content in and out. The engine also draws only vertex colours with Lambert light: no textures, no sky, no specular. The Kula look in SPEC.md needs all three.

## Solution

The engine gains the Pack: a named set of assets that load and unload together. A game sends Load with a pack name and a list of asset names, and the host calls the new seam function loaded with the ids. The game sends Unload when it is done with a pack. "Level" becomes a game word; the engine has no level.

The renderer reads glTF base colour textures and metallic-roughness materials and lights them with a GGX BRDF. A Scene can name a cubemap sky. Kula uses one pack per Theme, swaps packs between three levels, and draws textured blocks under a Theme sky.

## User Stories

1. As a game author, I want to name the assets a pack holds in Roc, so that my game data decides what loads together.
2. As a game author, I want to load a pack with a Command, so that I can change content while the game runs.
3. As a game author, I want to unload a pack by name, so that memory frees when I no longer need its assets.
4. As a game author, I want several packs loaded at once, so that a world pack and a room pack can live together.
5. As a game author, I want to unload packs in any order, so that streamed chunks behind the player can go first.
6. As a game author, I want an asset named by two packs to load once and keep one id, so that shared assets cost nothing extra.
7. As a game author, I want a shared asset to stay loaded until its last pack unloads, so that unloading one pack never breaks another.
8. As a game author, I want loaded called with the pack name and its manifest, so that I know exactly when ids exist.
9. As a game author, I want loaded to run before the next view, so that a swap never draws a stale id.
10. As a game author, I want every name I asked for to appear in the manifest, so that I always get an answer.
11. As a game author, I want a missing or broken asset to get id 0 and one log line, so that a typo is visible, not fatal.
12. As a game author, I want init to return Commands, so that I can load my first pack before the first step.
13. As a game author, I want Config to list the asset names found on disk, so that I can check names in init.
14. As a game author, I want a Load for a loaded pack to log once and do nothing, so that a repeated Command is harmless.
15. As a game author, I want an Unload for an unknown pack to log once and do nothing, so that a stray Command is harmless.
16. As a game author, I want assets organised by type on disk, not by pack, so that one file can serve many packs.
17. As a game author, I want a stale id to draw the fallback, so that a bug shows as magenta instead of the wrong mesh.
18. As a game author, I want the primitives available with no pack, so that a game can draw before any load.
19. As an artist, I want the glTF base colour texture drawn, so that my Blender materials show in game.
20. As an artist, I want the glTF sampler honoured (nearest or linear, wrap, mipmaps), so that pixel art stays sharp and distant surfaces do not shimmer.
21. As an artist, I want base colour textures treated as sRGB, so that colours match Blender.
22. As an artist, I want baseColorFactor to multiply the texture, so that glTF materials combine as the spec says.
23. As an artist, I want roughness and metallic factors and the metallic-roughness texture read, so that shiny and matte parts look right.
24. As an artist, I want a mesh with no material to stay matte grey, so that primitives and plain meshes never turn into black metal.
25. As an artist, I want KHR_materials_unlit honoured, so that a sign or a glow draws at its authored colour.
26. As an artist, I want a JPEG texture skipped with a log, so that I know to export PNG.
27. As a player, I want highlights on the ball, so that it reads as a shiny sphere.
28. As a player, I want metal surfaces to keep their colour in shade, so that they do not go black without an environment map.
29. As a game author, I want light colours in physical units, so that glTF lights and engine lights mean the same thing.
30. As a game author, I want point lights to fall off with inverse square inside their range, so that they match glTF and Filament.
31. As a game author, I want to name a cubemap sky in my Scene, so that the background fits my world.
32. As a game author, I want sky 0 to mean no sky, so that the host clears to black.
33. As an artist, I want the sky drawn at its authored colour, so that the tone map does not darken it.
34. As an artist, I want a sky as six PNGs named px, nx, py, ny, pz, nz, so that common tools export it directly.
35. As a Kula player, I want each level to have its own Theme, so that the three levels look different.
36. As a Kula player, I want finishing a level to start the next after a short pause, so that the game flows.
37. As a Kula player, I want finishing level 3 to end in Won, so that the game has an end.
38. As a Kula player, I want the level change to show no magenta, so that the swap is clean.
39. As a Kula author, I want a Theme record to hold its pack, asset names, lights and sun, so that one table defines a world.
40. As a Kula author, I want textures and skies generated by scripts, so that no original assets enter the repo.
41. As an engine maintainer, I want the pack lifecycle tested through the host-game seam, so that the tests check behaviour, not internals.
42. As an engine maintainer, I want each asset table to reuse freed slots safely, so that streaming never runs out of slots early.

## Implementation Decisions

Packs and the seam:
- Pack is the engine term. CONTEXT.md and docs/GLOSSARY.md gain Pack; Level leaves the engine vocabulary and goes in Pack's Avoid list. ADR 0003 records "Packs own asset lifetimes".
- Command gains Load({ pack : Str, assets : List(Str) }) and Unload(Str).
- init changes to Config -> { model, commands }.
- A fourth seam function: loaded : Model, Str, Manifest -> Model. Manifest is List({ name : Str, id : U32 }).
- Config carries assets : List(Str), the names found on disk, with no ids. Mesh names are file stems from assets/meshes/. Sky names are sky/<dir> from assets/sky/.
- The host runs each Command after the step that returned it and before view. Load is synchronous, and loaded runs in the same frame. loaded is the only promise that ids exist, so a later background loader changes no game.
- A swap is Load(new), then loaded, then Unload(old) from a later step.
- Only the primitives load at startup. They belong to no pack and never unload.
- Packs are independent. Any number load, and each unloads by name in any order.
- An asset named by several loaded packs loads once and keeps one id. Each asset counts the packs that hold it and unloads at zero.
- GPU resources belong to the asset. Vertex and image data are scratch until upload, so a pack keeps only its name and its asset list.
- The mesh table (64 slots) and a new sky table (16 slots, slot 0 means no sky) use the existing slot-and-generation id and a free list.
- A name not on disk, or a file that fails, gets id 0 in the manifest and one log line.
- Load of a loaded pack, Unload of an unknown pack, and a second Load of one pack in one step each log once per pack name and do nothing.
- The level arena and level_unload are renamed for packs or removed. mesh_table_unload_level becomes per-pack unload.

Textures and materials:
- Vertex gains uv. One vertex format and one pipeline. A mesh with no texture binds a 1x1 white image. The primitives get UVs.
- The glTF loader reads TEXCOORD_0, the base colour texture (PNG from the GLB binary chunk via core:image/png), its sampler, metallicFactor, roughnessFactor, the metallic-roughness texture (G roughness, B metallic, linear) and KHR_materials_unlit. JPEG is skipped with a log.
- glTF defaults apply (both factors 1.0), except that a primitive with no material is grey, metallic 0, roughness 1.
- Base colour and sky images upload as SRGB8A8. Mipmaps are built on the CPU with a 2x2 box filter in linear light, only when the minification filter asks.
- baseColorFactor stays in the vertex colour and multiplies the texture.
- fs_params gains a per-mesh material vec4: roughness, metallic, unlit, spare. The host fills it from the mesh. The Draw does not change.
- The fragment shader gains the camera position.

Lighting:
- BRDF: GGX distribution, height-correlated Smith visibility, Schlick Fresnel with F0 = mix(0.04, base, metallic), Lambert diffuse (1 - metallic) * base / pi. alpha = roughness squared; roughness clamps to at least 0.045. Guard the half vector and every denominator, and write pow(1 - x, 5) as multiplies.
- Ambient: ambient * ((1 - metallic) * base + EnvBRDFApprox(F0, roughness, n.v)), after Karis (2014).
- Light colours follow physical units, with the 1/pi in the BRDF. Every game retunes its lights by pi. DESIGN.md states the convention.
- A point light keeps the windowed falloff and gains 1 / max(d^2, 0.01^2).
- The tint multiplies base colour only. Specular takes no tint.
- No exposure knob. Exposure belongs to the look record proposal (yjtqgdd4).
- Check every BRDF constant against the glTF 2.0 spec Appendix B, Filament and Karis before use. The research that chose them was not checked against those sources.

Sky and unlit:
- Scene gains sky : U32, 0 meaning none.
- The host draws a unit cube around the camera, pinned to the far plane (reversed Z), after the opaque pass.
- The sky and unlit meshes skip the lights and the tone map and draw their texture colour through the sRGB encode.

Kula:
- A kula pack, loaded from init, holds the ball and the assets every Theme shares.
- Three Themes, one per level. A Theme record holds its pack name, asset names, lights and sun direction. A table in Kula code maps each level to its Theme.
- Finishing level N sends Load for Theme N+1. On loaded, Kula switches its ids and starts the level; the next step sends Unload for the old pack. Finishing level 3 keeps Won.
- Levels 2 and 3 are hand-written .txt files in the existing format.
- make_meshes.py packs Blender-made PNG textures into each face .glb, sets UVs and metallic 0, and gives the ball a low roughness. A sibling Blender script renders six sky PNGs per Theme. The outputs are committed. No original assets.

Order: (1) Pack term and docs, (2) seam: Commands, loaded, init commands, Config names, glue, port cards, entity-game and Kula, (3) host tables: free lists, refcounts, packs, (4) textures and PBR, (5) sky, (6) Kula content. Steps 1 to 3 change nothing on screen. Steps 4 and 5 each need only step 3.

## Testing Decisions

- A good test drives behaviour through the highest seam and checks what a game or the screen would see, not table internals.
- The pack lifecycle is tested through the host-game seam with the fake game (prior art: seam_test.odin, including the command-before-view test) and a temporary assets directory (prior art: temp_mesh_dir in mesh_load_test.odin). Cover: init Load, loaded before view, a swap with no stale id, a shared asset's refcount, a missing name with id 0, and each nonsense Command logged once.
- glTF reading is tested with GLB bytes built in test code (prior art: gltf_test.odin): UVs, an embedded PNG, the sampler, the material factors, the defaults and the unlit extension.
- Image preparation is tested as plain procedures: PNG decode, sRGB format choice, linear-light mipmap sizes and values.
- Frame render is tested through its capture (prior art: frame_render_test.odin): the per-mesh material values and the sky draw.
- Kula is tested with Roc expect: the Theme table, and the order Load, loaded, then Unload in the next step.
- The shaders are checked by eye: each game runs under ROCCO_EXIT_AFTER_FRAMES and a person looks at the result. The GPU upload is not unit-tested; tests keep zero buffer ids and the destroy guard.
- The full suite runs once at the end of each task: odin test engine, host-check.sh, each game's roc test and the build script tests.

## Out of Scope

- Pong. ntbh6adj brings it back in line and includes the pack seam.
- Background loading. The seam allows it; the host loads synchronously.
- Runtime-generated assets sent from Roc.
- Image-based lighting, sky reflections, hemisphere ambient, normal maps, emissive and occlusion.
- An exposure knob and a choice of tone map (yjtqgdd4).
- Shadows (Milestone 13), the HUD (Milestone 14), fog (s1zhf2hf) and the pickup flash (nafp0q3s).
- Raising MESH_CAPACITY.

## Further Notes

- Part of 'The second arc' (docs/ROADMAP.md). Blocked by Milestone 11, which is done.
- jzvojfn9 (mesh id generation) is done. Its mesh_table_unload_level is the start of step 3.
- The Kula SPEC.md Theme definition ("a sky, a set of lights and a set of block meshes") maps directly to a pack plus a lights record.

Kula plays three levels, each in its own Theme pack with a textured face and a Blender-rendered sky. User checked all three levels by eye on 2026-10-15: no magenta.

name: Engine: scale a Draw along a world axis
description:
Triage: needs-triage
Type: grilling

## Question

How does a Draw squash a spinning mesh along a world axis? Kula needs this for the idle bob (ekx01utd) and for the jump stretch (42fsutrf).

## What exists

- The host builds the model matrix as T * R * S (engine/transform.odin). Draw.scale acts in model space, before rot.
- The Kula ball's rot is its spin. A model-space scale therefore squashes along an axis that spins with the ball.
- The original builds Orient * Morph * Spin (kula-world-decomp player_movement.c:1025-1027). The morph acts in the ball's frame, after the spin.
- T * R * S cannot express Orient * Morph * Spin for a non-uniform Morph.
- basic.glsl transforms normals by the model matrix, not by its inverse transpose. For the bob's scale (1.05, 1.05, 0.9) a 45 degree normal is off by about 9 degrees.

## Options

1. Add a scale frame to Draw: model = T * R * F * S * F^-1. F is a Quat. It defaults to identity.
2. Add a world-space squash to Draw, an axis and an amount, applied after R.
3. Let Draw carry a full 3x3 linear part in place of rot and scale. This loses the slerp of rot between Scenes.

Each option changes the vocabulary, the glue and the Draw interpolation. docs/DESIGN.md section 3 governs.

## Done when

- DESIGN.md records the choice.
- The shader uses the inverse transpose for normals, or the docs say why not.
result: Option 1: Draw.scale_rot. Model = T*R*F*S*F^-1; the host slerps F. The shader uses normal_model, the inverse transpose. DESIGN.md 'A scale acts along its own axes' and ADR 0002 record it.

commit.message: feat(engine): Scale a Draw along scale_rot and copy the Kula idle bob - Draw gains scale_rot. The model is T * R * F * S * F^-1, and the host slerps F between Scenes. - The shader lights normals with the inverse transpose. engine/transform.odin is gone. - linalg adds Quat.conjugate and Quat.between. Every game sends Quat.identity for scale_rot. - Kula squashes the ball along up at the full-clock rate, 2.05 s a bob, and keeps it on the floor. - DESIGN.md, CONTEXT.md, SPEC.md and ADR 0002 record the scale frame and the bob.

name: Kula: copy the idle bob
description:
Triage: needs-triage
Type: task

## What to build

The ball squashes and stretches about its up axis while it is not in a forward jump. games/kula/SPEC.md "Idle bob" states the rule.

- Ball keeps a bob phase in turns. Each step advances it by (165 - 1.25 * seconds left) * 50/4096 turns a second.

- The phase holds during a forward jump and during the edge wrap. The shape holds its last value.
- Leave the landing squish to 42fsutrf. Keep s separate so that task can add to it.

- The bob plays in the running game.
- SPEC.md moves the idle bob out of "Not copied".

name: Kula: jump in place and the forward-jump rules
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent

The original has two kinds of jump. The clone has only the forward jump, and Space always starts it. Copy the original. See the Jump section of games/kula/SPEC.md, read from the decompilation 2026-10-13. Decided with the user 2026-10-13: copy the original on every open point.

## Requirements

Jump kinds:
1. Space while the ball is still and Up is not held starts a jump in place. The ball rises and lands on the same cell, with the same duration and peak as the forward jump. The pose does not change, apart from turns.
2. Space while Up is held starts a forward jump, as now.
3. Space during a floor roll starts a forward jump at once, from the ball's current position. Climbs and turns cannot start a jump. Changed with the user 2026-10-14: an edge roll can start a forward jump until the ball reaches the edge, as in the original (HandleViewportRotationStart). The jump starts from the roll's from cell.
   - The landing cell is two cells ahead of the cell the ball is nearest to: the roll's from cell when t < 0.5, else its target cell.
   - View moves the ball from its current interpolated position to the landing cell.
   - Keys collect on commit, so a key in the roll's target cell is already collected.
4. Bounces: a block above bounces both kinds. A block one or two cells ahead bounces only the forward jump. A bounced ball does not move, as now.

Mid-air input:
5. No input acts during a forward jump.
6. During a jump in place, Left and Right turn the ball. The turn takes 0.32 s and can outlast the jump. A turn press during a turn starts that turn when the current one ends (the original's startTurningLeftNextFrame).

Landing:
7. The landing check runs in the last 11 of 27 frames (t >= 16/27). The ball lands when its centre is at or below rest height over a floor. On level ground this is t = 1. Add an expect that shows the window.
8. If Up is held when a jump lands, the next roll starts in the same step, with no rest step. Use the same rule when a roll ends with Up held, which also fixes item 2 of 0v9t9lz3.

Docs:
9. Update the Clone column of the Jump table in SPEC.md and the Moves and Controls sections of games/kula/README.md.

## Not in scope

- The long jump, the Bouncy pill and bounce pads (SPEC.md, Long jump).
- The jump's height and frame count. They are in GGI data, not the C code.
- The sideways snap of AutoAlignJumpStartPos. The clone's ball is always on the cell line.

## Done when

- roc test games/kula/main.roc passes, with an expect for each requirement 1 to 8.
- By hand on arm64mac: Space alone hops in place, Up+Space jumps the level1 gap, Space mid-roll jumps at once, Left during a hop turns the ball, and held Up rolls without a pause through cells and after a landing.
result: Jump in place, forward-jump rules, mid-air turns with a turn queue, the landing window and held-Up roll chaining. Edge rolls can start a forward jump before the edge (changed with the user 2026-10-14). Checked by hand by the user.

name: Simplify the macOS sysroot script to keep the SDK layout
description:
Rewrite scripts/make-macos-sysroot.sh so that it copies SDK framework stubs with their real layout. Remove the re-export stripping and the objc.framework trick.

Why: the header of the script is wrong for Roc nightly-2026-09-12-220fd47. An LLD_REPRODUCE capture of 'roc build' shows that Roc passes -syslibroot platform/targets/macos-sysroot, -F <sysroot>/System/Library/Frameworks, -L <sysroot>/usr/lib and -lSystem. Re-exports failed only because the script writes a flat Foo.framework/Foo.tbd. lld resolves each re-export by its install name under the syslibroot, for example AppKit.framework/Versions/C/AppKit.tbd.

Evidence from the experiment:
- Sysroot = the Xcode SDK itself: the link fails. Roc emits one -framework per framework in the sysroot. QTKit and JavaNativeFoundation are Intel-only, SwiftUICore refuses clients, and Message does not resolve. So the script must still pick the frameworks.
- Sysroot = the 16-framework closure copied with 'cp -R -P' from the SDK (Versions/ and symlinks kept, nothing stripped), plus usr/lib/libSystem*.tbd and usr/lib/libobjc*.tbd, and no objc.framework: the link passes and bodies.bin runs. otool -L shows /usr/lib/libobjc.A.dylib, linked through the Foundation re-export.

Steps:
1. Keep the closure walk over reexported-libraries. Re-exported frameworks must exist in the sysroot, or lld cannot resolve them.
2. For each framework in the closure, copy only the .tbd files and the symlinks that point to them: Foo.framework/Foo.tbd -> Versions/Current/Foo.tbd, Versions/Current -> <V>, and Versions/<V>/Foo.tbd. Do not copy Headers or Modules. A full 'cp -R -P' copy is 33 MB, mostly headers.
3. Copy usr/lib/libSystem.tbd, libSystem.B.tbd, libobjc.tbd and libobjc.A.tbd, with their symlinks.
4. Delete strip_reexports and the objc.framework block.
5. Rewrite the header comment. Keep one real constraint: Roc links every framework in the sysroot, so the sysroot holds only the frameworks the host needs.
6. Run 'roc scripts/build.roc -- all' from an empty platform/targets/macos-sysroot and run examples/bodies.

Done when examples/bodies links and runs with the new sysroot, 'otool -L examples/bodies/bodies.bin' lists /usr/lib/libobjc.A.dylib, and the script has no stripping code.

Related: a Zulip question asks whether a platform header can name its frameworks. If Roc adds that, the sysroot can become the SDK path and this script can go.

name: Emit non-recursive tag unions from the Odin glue
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent
Type: task

Work in the roc-odin-glue repo (the glue/ submodule, also checked out at ~/playground/roc-odin-glue). Commit there, then bump the submodule here. The Zig glue is the reference: ~/playground/odin-game-engine/ZigGlue.roc (union emission about lines 900-1080).

Requirements:
- Emit a union with payloads as three types:
    <Name>_Tag :: enum uN { ... }
    <Name>_Payload :: struct #raw_union { <snake_tag>: T, ... }
    <Name> :: struct { payload: <Name>_Payload, _padN: [n]u8, tag: <Name>_Tag }
  Do not use Odin's union.
- Take the discriminant width from AbiLayout discriminant_size(). Take the tag values from the tu.tags order. Order multi-field payloads by payload_fields (alignment order), as the Zig glue does.
- Assert size, alignment and offset_of(tag) == discriminant_offset(Pointer64).
- Emit a union with no payloads as a bare enum uN, with no struct.
- Name a union by its field path, the same walk as records (for example Roc_View_Colliders_Shape). Use tu.name when it is present.
- Teach walk, reach and odin_type to follow RocTagUnion payloads.
- Crash with a clear message that names the type for a recursive union, and for a union payload that needs refcounting (List, Str, Box). release_proc must not silently treat such a union as Flat.
- Emit the 64-bit layout only. No accessors or constructors.
- Add a fixture glue/example/unions/ with one type per case: no payloads, one payload per tag, a multi-field payload, a nested union, a union in a record and a union in a list. check.sh diffs it against expected, builds it with -vet -strict-style, and runs an odin test that checks the layout.
- README: remove non-recursive tag unions from the unimplemented list. Keep recursive unions and refcounted union payloads on it.

Done when:
- glue/example/check.sh passes with the new fixture;
- the submodule bump here leaves engine/roc_platform_abi.odin unchanged (Collider has no union yet) and host-check passes.
result: OdinGlue emits non-recursive tag unions (glue 93aaaee): a tag enum, a payload raw union and a struct with the tag at its committed offset, or a bare enum for unions with no payloads. Anonymous unions take path names; the compiler names them by joining tags with Or, so only a := union keeps tu.name. Recursive, single-tag and refcounted-payload unions crash with the type's name. example/unions covers each case with a layout test. Engine glue is unchanged and host-check passes. roc glue caches by platform and can return an older spec's output; check.sh uses --no-cache.

name: Milestone 14: the HUD
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent
Type: task

Done when the key count changes on screen without a 3D draw. A box that floats to a corner stays there when the window resizes, and the count reads right at two window sizes.

Decided in the Milestone 14 grilling on 2026-10-15. ADR 0004 records "UI layout runs in the host". CONTEXT.md defines UI, Element, Box, Text and Rgba.

## Problem Statement

A game can draw only meshes in 3D. It cannot put a number, a word or a panel flat on the screen. Kula needs to show the keys collected. Later games need menus and inventories with nested layouts.

## Solution

Scene gains ui : List(Element), a flat stream of Open(Box), Text and Close. The host feeds the stream to C Clay once per frame, against the window size. The host measures text with one baked SDF font and draws Clay's render commands as one batch of quads inside the Main pass. Games write nested code with packages/ui/, which builds the stream. Kula shows "Keys 1 / 2" in a panel at the top-left.

## User Stories

1. As a game author, I want to put text and boxes on screen from view, so that my UI is a Description like my Draws.
2. As a game author, I want to write nested boxes in Roc, so that I do not write Open and Close by hand.
3. As a game author, I want to anchor a box to a corner of the window, so that it stays there when the window resizes.
4. As a game author, I want Clay's sizing (Fit, Grow, Fixed, Percent), padding, gap, direction and child alignment, so that my layouts can grow past a key count.
5. As a game author, I want a background colour with alpha and a corner radius, so that a panel can sit over the 3D view.
6. As a game author, I want Text at any size and colour, so that I do not choose from fixed font sizes.
7. As a game author, I want an empty Box config to mean what Clay means, so that defaults do not surprise me.
8. As a game author, I want unbalanced Open and Close to log once and still draw, so that a bug is visible, not fatal.
9. As a game author, I want a character the font does not have to draw as "?" and log once, so that I see the gap.
10. As a player, I want the UI drawn sharp and at its authored colour, so that the tone map does not change it.
11. As a Kula player, I want to see the keys collected out of the total, so that I know how many are left.
12. As an engine maintainer, I want Clay pinned as a submodule and copied by the inputs step, so that updates are one command.
13. As an engine maintainer, I want the font baked by a build step into a committed Odin file, so that the build needs no font tool.
14. As an engine maintainer, I want no allocation per frame for the UI, so that the frame cost stays fixed.
15. As an engine maintainer, I want the corner anchor tested at two window sizes through Frame_Render's capture, so that the milestone check is automatic.

## Implementation Decisions

Vocabulary:
- Rgba : { r, g, b, a }, linear channels from 0 to 1, alpha not premultiplied. Tint stays Rgb.
- Element : [Open(Box), Text(Text), Close]. The union is not recursive, so the glue carries it. An Element's identity is its place in the list.
- Box: width and height as [Fit({ min, max }), Grow({ min, max }), Fixed(F32), Percent(F32)], pad { left, right, top, bottom }, gap, direction [Row, Col], child_align { x, y } as [Start, Center, End], background : Rgba, radius : F32 (one value), floating [NoFloat, Float({ attach : AttachPoint, offset })]. AttachPoint has Clay's nine names, LeftTop to RightBottom. A Box floats to the window root only.
- Text: the string, size, color : Rgba, wrap [Words, None].
- Names and defaults follow Clay (Fit, Start), so an empty config means the same on both sides.
- Scene gains ui : List(Element). Every game adds ui: [], except pong (ntbh6adj).
- The game does not learn the window size. Sizes are logical pixels. The host multiplies by sapp.dpi_scale(), which is 1 while high_dpi is off.
- The UI is a Description. The host draws the current Scene's UI only, with no interpolation.

Host:
- Clay enters as a git submodule pinned to a commit. The inputs step copies its prebuilt lib from bindings/odin/clay-odin/ per target, like sokol's. platform/main.roc lists it per target. arm64mac and x64glibc only. If a prebuilt lib fails on a target, compile clay.h for that target in the inputs step.
- The Clay arena comes from perm at init, sized by MinMemorySize() with the default element cap.
- The host lays out once per frame against sapp.width() and sapp.height(), from the current Scene. It walks the stream in order: Open calls open and configure, Text adds text, Close closes.
- A Close with no open Box is ignored. Boxes still open at the end are closed. Each logs once.
- A Clay error logs once per kind and the host draws what fits.
- Text strings point into the current Scene, which lives for the frame, so the host copies no string.
- The measure callback uses the baked metrics. One font, so the font id is always 0.
- A character outside ASCII 32 to 126 draws as "?" and logs once.

Drawing:
- The UI draws inside the Main pass, after the sky, with its own pipeline: no depth test, no depth write, alpha blend, sample count 4.
- Every rectangle and glyph goes into one dynamic vertex buffer per frame, sized at init (about 16k quads). One draw call per scissor or texture change. Past the cap, the host drops the rest and logs once.
- A new ui program in engine/shaders/basic.glsl draws rounded rectangles and SDF glyphs with smoothstep. Colours are linear, skip the tone map, and go through the sRGB encode, like the sky.
- Frame_Render owns the UI pass, and its capture adapter records the quads.

Font:
- One SDF atlas, ASCII 32 to 126, from Atkinson Hyperlegible (OFL). The .ttf and its licence are committed under scripts/fonts/.
- A Font step in scripts/build.roc runs an Odin bake tool that uses vendor:stb/truetype (stbtt_GetCodepointSDF). It writes engine/font_baked.odin with a "Generated, do not edit" header. If the tool cannot run, the committed file stays, as for shader_basic.odin.

packages/ui/:
- Nested helpers such as box(config, children) and text(str, style) flatten to the Element stream.
- A default Box config with Clay's defaults.

Kula:
- Hud.roc builds the UI: a Box floating at LeftTop with offset 16, background Rgba with a = 0.5, radius 8. Inside it, Text "Keys n / total" at size 24 in white. n is collected.len() and total is keys_left + collected.len().
- The HUD shows in every phase. No level number and no win banner.
- The README gains "keys collected". The word "held" stays for Input.

## Testing Decisions

- The corner anchor is tested through Frame_Render's capture with a fake game's Scene: a box floating at RightBottom, checked at two window sizes.
- Stream errors are tested through the same seam: an unbalanced Open, an extra Close and the quad cap, each logged once.
- The font measure is a plain procedure, tested against known metrics, including the "?" fallback.
- packages/ui/ is tested with Roc expect: nested helpers give the right stream.
- Kula is tested with Roc expect: Hud gives "Keys 1 / 2" after one key is collected.
- The shader and blending are checked by eye: scripts/screenshot.sh kula at 960x540 and at a second size.
- The Linux container run exits 0.
- The full suite runs once at the end of each task: odin test engine, host-check.sh, each game's roc test and the build script tests.

## Out of Scope

- high_dpi (follow-up task).
- Pointer input, hover and clicks (follow-up task; reopens ADR 0004).
- Images in a Box, borders, per-corner radius, scroll, clip, z-index, floating to another element, letter spacing and line height.
- Fonts that a game provides (kf5vd0lp).

name: Kula Ball and View: rolls, turns, climbs, edge rolls, jumps, camera follows
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent

The ball rolls, turns, climbs, rolls round edges and jumps, and the camera
follows. See the decisions in Milestone 10 (72omk38x). Grilled 2026-10-13.

## Requirements

Ball.roc:
1. `Ball : { pose : Pose, motion : Motion, rot : Quat }` with `Motion :
[Still, Rolling({ from : Pose, t : F32 }), Turning({ from : Pose, t : F32 }),
Jumping({ from : Pose, t : F32 })]`. Add Falling in the Rules ticket.
2. The pose commits when a move starts. `from` and `t` exist for View only.
Input is read only when Still.
3. `roll : Set(Cell), Pose -> Try(Pose, [ClosedEdge])` checks three cases
in order:
   a. Block at cell + forward: climb. cell stays, up' = -forward,
   forward' = up.
   b. Block at cell + forward - up: floor. cell' = cell + forward.
   c. Else: edge. cell' = cell + forward - up, up' = forward, forward' = -up.
   Case c needs an open end: Err(ClosedEdge) when a block sits left or
   right of the block at cell - up, as in the original.
   One expect per case. Case c is the milestone check.
4. `turn_left` and `turn_right` rotate forward a quarter turn about up with
Grid.cross. One expect each.
5. `jump : Set(Cell), Pose -> [Land(Pose), Fall(Pose), Bounce]`. Bounce when
a block sits at cell + up, cell + forward or cell + 2 forward. Land at
cell + 2 forward when a block sits at cell + 2 forward - up. Otherwise Fall
at cell + 2 forward. A jump never lands on the block ahead; the original
only climbs by rolling. Expects cover each outcome.
6. Timing from the original's PAL frame counts: a floor roll takes 0.26 s,
a climb 0.28 s, an edge roll 0.34 s, a turn 0.32 s, a jump 0.54 s. `advance : Ball,
F32 -> Ball` moves t and returns Still when t reaches 1.
7. Input: Up held starts the next roll on the step the current motion ends.
Left and Right act on press only. Space on press jumps. Key codes from
pf.Key; the binding lives in main.roc.
8. rot accumulates each step while Rolling: axis = cross(up, forward), angle
= distance / radius with radius 0.195, through Quat.mul. The distance is 1
for a floor roll, 2 (0.5 - radius) for a climb and 1 + radius pi / 2 for an
edge roll. A jump does not spin.

View.roc:
9. `interpolated : Ball -> { pos : Vec3, up : Vec3, forward : Vec3 }` lerps
from `from` to `pose` by t with Vec3.lerp; up and forward are normalised. A
jump adds a parabola of height 0.5 along up.
10. The ball's draw centre is pos - (0.5 - radius) up, scale 2 radius, with
rot. The centre rests 0.195 cell above the face. Round an edge the centre
goes half a cell to the edge, a quarter circle of one radius about the edge
line, then half a cell down the side, so the ball never enters the block.
11. Camera: the original's view space. The basis is the ball's frame pitched
down 250/4096 of a turn. The ball centre sits 250/512 below the view axis at
a depth of 800/512. vFOV 1.286 rad. No smoothing, no clipping test. After a
climb the eye sits inside the floor the ball left.
11a. Blocks draw as exposed faces: one primitive plane per face that borders
an empty cell. No face between two blocks. The one-sided planes are why the
floor does not hide the ball after a climb.
Changed 2026-10-13 from a fixed offset; see games/kula/SPEC.md.

main.roc:
12. step runs stages in order: read input, advance motion, (rules later),
then returns commands. Each stage is a function Model -> Model.
13. Model gains the Ball. init builds it from Level.start.

## Not in scope

- No keys, exit, win or falling. Fall returns a Pose and nothing acts on it
yet.
- No .glb meshes.

## Done when

- `roc test games/kula/main.roc` passes, with expects for the three roll
cases, both turns, every jump outcome, the timing and rot accumulation.
- By hand on arm64mac: the ball rolls over an edge onto the side of a block
and keeps rolling, and the camera follows round the edge.
result: Ball rolls, climbs, wraps edges and jumps two cells; the camera and block faces follow the original's numbers in games/kula/SPEC.md. Checked by hand on arm64mac.

name: Choose the tone map per game
description:
Triage: needs-triage
Type: grilling

Today the shader applies one fixed ACES fit (65wor4ep, no knob). AgX keeps saturated highlights from shifting hue. Khronos PBR Neutral keeps material colours closest to their authored values. A game could choose one.

Config goes from the host to the game, so it cannot carry the choice. Options:
1. A Scene field, such as tone_map : [Aces, AgX, Neutral]. A Theme can change it per level.
2. A one-time Command at start-up.

Recommendation: a Scene field. Lights are already Scene data. Fog (s1zhf2hf) also wants a Scene field. Consider one Scene record for the look, such as exposure, tone map and fog, so Scene does not gain one field for each effect.

The host passes an int in fs_params and the fragment shader branches on it.

name: Game-level engine settings
description:
Triage: needs-triage
Type: grilling

Nothing goes from the game to the host at start-up. Config goes the other way.
Settings come in two kinds:
1. Start-up settings set GPU resources and cannot change per frame: shadow map
size, shadow bias, soft-shadow mode (PCF or PCSS), cascade count. A project
file such as games/<game>/rocco.toml fits them. The host reads it before init.
2. Look settings can change per level: tone map, fog, exposure. One Scene
record fits them.

Decide both homes in one grilling. Related: yjtqgdd4 (tone map), s1zhf2hf
(fog). Milestone 13 (cxtqbqrl) uses host constants until this lands.

Milestone 13 result: the Kula shadow edge looks a little soft. The edge width
comes from SHADOW_MAP_SIZE over the size of the box around the level, and from
the 3x3 PCF kernel. Expose both, so a game can trade sharpness for cost.

name: Vec3 package: packages/linalg and the entity game uses it
description:
Triage: ready-for-agent

decisions in Milestone 10 (72omk38x). Grilled 2026-10-13.

packages/linalg on 2026-10-13 (eebe0aa), so Quat can join it and import Vec3.

1. Create packages/linalg/main.roc with header `package [Vec3] {}` and
packages/linalg/Vec3.roc as a type module, the same layout as packages/camera.
2. Vec3.roc declares its own structural `Vec3 : { x : F32, y : F32, z : F32 }`.
Inside the type module, annotations name it `Vec3.Vec3`. No package depends
on another package.
3. Expose zero, one, add, sub, neg, scale, dot, cross, length, normalize and
lerp. `lerp : Vec3, Vec3, F32 -> Vec3`. `normalize` of zero returns zero.

add, scale and dot. Keep rotate_y and pi; the quaternion ticket removes
rotate_y.
6. Run `roc test examples/entity-game/main.roc` and `roc test
packages/linalg/main.roc`.

## Not in scope

- No change to platform/Vocabulary.roc. The vocabulary keeps its own Vec3.
- No change to packages/camera or packages/mesh.
- No rotate or quaternion function.

## Done when

- Both test runs pass.
- `roc scripts/build.roc -- game entity-game` builds and the game runs as
before on arm64mac.
- scripts/alloc-check.sh still reports 3 for entity-game.
